gate: SELECTOR_SERVICE_V1 - one request end to end: ServiceRequest -> Selector V1 -> ExecutionPlan -> existing runner -> pass -> P2 -> retry at higher p -> DECIDED or a legitimate STOP / REFUSED
classification: FCC_N SCENARIO FAMILY - NOT THE 2/3-ATOM CERTIFICATION SCOPE

baseline.this_branch: claude/selector-service-v1 in the main checkout (no worktree); working tree clean at start
baseline.existing_evidence_diff: none (docs/active and experiments unchanged since their result commits)
baseline.desktop_topology: 12 logical / 6 physical, SMT pairs (2k, 2k+1) - not used for the campaign
baseline.laptop_topology: 6 physical cores, one logical CPU each (0..5), no SMT (W5_PLACEMENT_V1 topology.json); rechecked by the campaign at start

pipeline: ServiceRequest{N, T, goal} -> loop: p = P2 (experiments/precision_pilot_a1/policies.next_p('P2', None, history, T), imported unchanged: first p = 64, then p2_next, P_MAX = 1024, 'CAP' when 1024 was already tried) -> Selector V1(N, T, p, goal, topology) -> ExecutionPlan -> experiments/w5_placement_v1/run (unchanged; CPU_SERIAL -> multiatom run_serial, CPU_PARALLEL -> e2_pair_parallel run_parallel, GPU refused) in a fresh process -> pass record -> history. Every pass recomputes the trajectory from step 0. Final when the pass outcome is DECIDED, DOMAIN_VIOLATED_PROVEN or OUT_OF_RANGE (STOP), or P2 returns CAP (REFUSED_AT_CAP). Safety bound 24 passes.
P3_not_used: P3 lines exist only for A2_bound / A3_low / A3_high; FCC_N has none. P3 is not used and not retrained.

selector_v1.forbidden_inputs: outcome of the current or any future pass, the true minimum p, verifier results, shadow results, timings

goals.WALL_MIN: frozen initial rule from the p = 128 data of MULTIATOM / E2_PAIR_PARALLEL: T = 100: N <= 4 SERIAL, 5 <= N < 12 W4, N >= 12 W6; T = 1000: N = 3 W3, N >= 4 W6

selector_v1.p_is_input_but_unused_in_V1: the worker count does not depend on p in V1; whether it should is measured (shadow)
selector_v1.domain: T in {100, 1000} only; T = 1000 with N < 3 and any N < 2 are outside the rule; topology must be 6 physical cores without SMT with one logical CPU per core (the laptop); anything else -> UNSUPPORTED_SELECTOR_DOMAIN (no pass is executed)
selector_v1.placement: main CPU 0, workers on CPUs 1..W for W <= 5, W6 = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0] (the W5_PLACEMENT_V1 layouts; serial on CPU 1)
selector_v1.not_production_truth: the rule is a hypothesis under test; it is not changed during this experiment whatever the results

evaluation_requests.why: none of these N were used to make the rule (3, 4, 6, 12, 24, 48)
evaluation_requests.pre_seal_cost_probe: laptop, serial E2, 10 steps (no outcome at T is visible from it): per step N=5 9.7/10.2/11.3 ms, N=8 26.9/28.0/31.3 ms, N=16 114/119/133 ms, N=32 469/489/547 ms at p = 64/128/256; one serial pass of all six requests ~ 110 s. No request removed.

strategies.SEL_WALL: the service with goal WALL_MIN (Selector V1)
strategies.SEL_CPU: the service with goal CPU_MIN; Selector V1 returns CPU_SERIAL at every pass, which is exactly the 'always SERIAL E2 + P2' baseline B, so SEL_CPU is run once and serves as baseline B (the checker verifies that every chosen plan is CPU_SERIAL)
strategies.FIXED_W6: baseline C: always W6 E2 + P2 (same service loop, plan fixed)

shadow.what: after the three service runs of a (request, repetition), for every p that the service tried, run the plans W3 and W4 (SERIAL and W6 at that p come from SEL_CPU and FIXED_W6) - so every tried (N, T, p) has SERIAL, W3, W4, W6 measured
shadow.isolation: shadow runs happen after the service runs, are stored separately and are never an input of the selector
shadow.order: per repetition: requests in the listed order; within a request the three strategies rotated by repetition index, then the shadow runs (W3, W4 alternated per p)

correctness.bit_identity: for every executed pass (all strategies, shadow, repetitions) at the same (N, T, p): outcome, completed_steps, stop, stop_step, cells, endpoints_key and initial-state digest identical to the CPU_SERIAL pass
correctness.same_p_sequence: SEL_WALL, SEL_CPU and FIXED_W6 of one request must try the same p sequence (it depends only on bit-identical outcomes)
correctness.checker_independence: the checker reimplements the P2 next-p rule and the Selector V1 table itself (it imports neither policies.py nor selector.py) and re-derives every next p from the recorded previous pass and every plan from the recorded selector input; DECIDED cells are re-derived from the stored endpoints with the A1 checker rounding
fault_injection_tests: selector input contains a future outcome
selector input contains the true minimum p
a GPU plan recorded as success

probes_in_evidence: the campaign also submits {N: 5, T: 500} (must be refused UNSUPPORTED_SELECTOR_DOMAIN with zero passes) and one GPU plan (must be refused, NotImplementedError, zero passes)
measurements: per pass: plan, selector input, requested/effective p, outcome, completed steps, stop, cells, endpoints, initial digest, end-to-end wall, loop wall, ready wall, total CPU (QueryProcessCycleTime / calibrated rate) and main / worker split, main breakdown, worker busy walls, affinities; per service run: total wall (all passes + orchestration), total CPU, number of passes, final status and p

analysis_questions.Q1: did every request end correctly (DECIDED with verified cells, or a legitimate STOP/REFUSED) under all strategies?
analysis_questions.Q2: CPU_MIN: was SERIAL the cheapest in total CPU per request (vs SEL_WALL, FIXED_W6, and per p vs W3/W4)?
analysis_questions.Q3: was SEL_WALL faster than SERIAL in total wall for every request?
analysis_questions.Q4: was SEL_WALL better than FIXED_W6 (wall, CPU, wall x CPU)?
analysis_questions.Q5: per (N, T): does the wall-best plan among {SERIAL, W3, W4, W6} change with p?
analysis_questions.Q6: does the p = 128 rule's choice equal the wall-best plan at every tried p?
analysis_questions.Q7: regret: SEL_WALL chosen-plan wall vs the per-p best plan wall, summed over the passes of each request (ratio)
analysis_questions.Q8: number of P2 passes per request and the p sequence
analysis_questions.Q9: cost split: precision-retry share = wall/CPU of non-final passes / total; parallel-overhead share = (parallel CPU - serial CPU at the same p) / parallel total CPU, and startup share of pass wall
analysis_questions.Q10: is there evidence to make p a real selector variable (does the best W differ between tried p for the same (N, T) by more than the repetition spread)?

noise_rule: a plan is 'wall-best' at (N, T, p) when its median end-to-end wall is lowest; a difference below 3 % of the best is reported as a TIE, not as a change of the best plan
cpu_cap: 12,000 CPU s (cycle-counted, all runs); the campaign stops at the next run boundary when exceeded
load_rule: E2_PAIR_PARALLEL_V1 / W5 rule: 1 s snapshot before every (request, repetition) group; CONTAMINATED if others >= 1 logical CPU or a python/roblox/codex/node process >= 25 %; contaminated groups are kept, checked for correctness and excluded from performance numbers
not_in_scope: changing the selector rule during the experiment
claims_forbidden: the V1 rule is production truth
a laptop result holds for SMT machines
a 1-3 % wall difference picks a winner
amendment_1_before_any_run: Before the code seal, on the desktop (scratch): (1) the checker fault-injection test fixture runs a real N = 5, T = 100 request (1 repetition, all three strategies + shadows) with the laptop topology map as selector input; its outcomes and timings were not looked at (the tests only assert which checks fail). (2) dry run with N = 3, T = 100 (not an evaluation request): P2 tried p 64 -> 105, DECIDED under all strategies, bit-identical, probes refused with zero passes; the sealed load rule flagged the desktop group as CONTAMINATED. (3) defect found by the dry run and fixed before the seal: analysis crashed when a request had no clean repetition; it now reports such a request as excluded. An ignore_load switch exists for dry runs only; the campaign analysis always honours the load rule. Nothing in the selector rule, requests, strategies, shadow scope, thresholds or cap changed.
